back: Self-government by ministers responsible to an elected colonial parliament, with Britain keeping some reserved powers.

front: What did the Land Apportionment Act (1930) do?
back: Divided land by race: about half (the best land and all towns) for Europeans; reserves and Native Purchase Areas for Africans.

front: What did the Industrial Conciliation Act (1934) do?
back: Excluded Africans from the definition of employee, keeping them out of registered unions and most apprenticeships.

front: What did the Native Land Husbandry Act (1951) do?
back: Enforced destocking, conservation works and individual land rights in the reserves.
The compulsory reduction of the number of cattle kept by African farmers.

front: Why did the reserved powers not protect Africans?
back: Britain never used its right to veto discriminatory laws.

front: Name two strikes by African workers under Responsible Government.
back: The railway workers' strike of 1945 and the general strike of 1948.

front: Who benefited from the Maize Control Act (1931)?
back: White farmers, who received the better local-market price; most African maize got the lower price.
